observations: The canonical Bank of England page resolved with the exact title “Why does money depend on trust?” and stated that it was last updated on 19 May 2020.

The directly observed body developed the barter and personal-IOU thought experiment, the problem of trust chains at scale, money as a widely accepted IOU, and the roles of genuine notes, anti-counterfeiting and broadly stable purchasing power.
The page visibly contained an embedded official video link and a transcript section. The full video was not played or tested.
The same canonical page and substantive body remained readable after publication.
scope_caveats: This is an introductory public explainer from the Bank of England and reflects its UK banknote and price-stability remit; it is not a complete survey of monetary theory, commercial-bank deposits, digital payments or cross-country institutions.
The embedded video, all linked pages and China-local playback or accessibility were not exhaustively tested.
The note summarizes structure and creates original practice; it does not reproduce the article or transcript.
